NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a thermal-gradient-compensated cell balancing system that actively adjusts balancing current based on localized temperature measurements to counteract the temperature-induced capacity and self-discharge variations across the module. Standard practice uses a fixed balancing algorithm regardless of temperature variations, while our mitigation introduces temperature-dependent balancing thresholds that dynamically adjust to maintain voltage spread within 35mV despite thermal gradients. This departs from existing battery management systems that either ignore thermal effects or use passive thermal management without balancing compensation. The closest existing practice is temperature-compensated state-of-charge estimation in EVs, but our approach is fundamentally different as it directly modifies balancing behavior rather than just recalibrating voltage-to-SOC mappings.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the temperature dependence of both capacity and self-discharge rate in lithium-ion cells: ΔC/C = α·ΔT and ΔSD/SD = β·ΔT, where α≈0.5%/°C and β≈7-10%/°C for NMC-811. With a 15°C gradient, this creates a capacity spread of ~7.5% and self-discharge spread of ~105-150%. By implementing temperature-dependent balancing thresholds that increase balancing current in warmer cells (which have higher self-discharge) and decrease it in cooler cells, we directly counteract these thermal effects. The magnitude verification shows that a 1 A balancing current can compensate for approximately 0.5-1% capacity difference per cycle, which is sufficient to counteract the thermal drift when applied differentially across temperature zones.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Temperature sensors: 13 NTC thermistors (±0.5°C accuracy) mounted directly on cell terminals (replaces existing single-module temperature sensor)
2. Microcontroller upgrade: Replacement of existing balancing controller with a temperature-aware version (same form factor, firmware-only change)
3. Balancing current adjustment circuit: 13 simple variable current sources using existing MOSFETs with temperature-dependent gate voltage (replaces fixed current sources)
4. Calibration data: Temperature-to-balancing-correction lookup table (developed from cell characterization data)
5. Installation procedure: Remove existing temperature sensor, mount 13 thermistors on cell terminals, replace balancing controller, upload new firmware, calibrate using thermal chamber test

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Temperature sensors: +13 thermistors vs 1 in standard practice (same cost class, standard components)
- Microcontroller: Same replacement cost as standard practice (existing hardware, firmware change only)
- Balancing circuit: Same MOSFETs as standard practice, with minor circuit modifications (no new hardware classes)
- Calibration data: One-time development cost, negligible per-unit impact
- Installation: Same labor as standard practice with additional thermistor mounting time (offset by elimination of single sensor calibration)
Burden class conclusion: Same burden class as standard practice. The added components are all standard, procurable items with no new hardware classes required. The development cost is a one-time engineering expense that doesn't affect the per-unit manufacturing cost class.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Subject 4 modules (2 test, 2 control) to accelerated aging with 15°C top-to-bottom thermal gradient cycling (0.5C charge/discharge, 25°C average temperature). Monitor cell voltages and temperatures continuously.
Instruments: Data acquisition system with 0.1 mV voltage resolution and 0.1°C temperature resolution, thermal chamber with gradient capability.
Pass/fail criterion: Test modules must maintain <35 mV voltage spread at rest after 1000 cycles (equivalent to 10 calendar years), while control modules exceed this threshold.
Duration: 1000 cycles or until failure, approximately 30 days continuous testing.
Kill criterion: If either test module exceeds 35 mV spread before 1000 cycles, the intervention is falsified. If control modules maintain <35 mV spread, the intervention is not validated (insufficient stress).
